evidence.paraphrase: The Flea reacts with bitterness to losing, complaining that merit is not rewarded.
evidence.quote: It's all the same to me," said the Flea. "She may have the old Leap-frog, for all I care. I jumped the highest; but in this world merit seldom meets its reward. A fine exterior is what people look at now-a-days.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator addresses the reader, noting the story may be untrue despite being printed.
evidence.quote: And then he began chirping his peculiar melancholy song, from which we have taken this history; and which may, very possibly, be all untrue, although it does stand here printed in black and white.

evidence.paraphrase: A claim that the Leap-frog's back can indicate whether winter will be severe or mild.
evidence.quote: the Leap-frog was a prophet; for that one could see on his back, if there would be a severe or mild winter, and that was what one could not see even on the back of the man who writes the almanac.
